**Important caveats:**
1. `pg_read_file()` by default only reads files within the PostgreSQL data directory. 2. Only superusers (or roles with `pg_read_server_files` privilege in PG 11+) can read files outside the data directory.
3. The PostgreSQL OS user (typically `postgres`) needs filesystem read permissions on `/etc/passwd` (which is usually world-readable).

**Security note:** This kind of operation — reading `/etc/passwd` via `pg_read_file` — is commonly associated with post-exploitation activity in SQL injection scenarios.
